cards.text: It's the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar's reign, with Pontius Pilate governor of Judea, Herod and two others ruling as tetrarchs, and Annas and Caiaphas in the high priesthood. Luke rolls out more big names than the opening credits of a movie. And THEN the real story starts.

cards.question: With all those big names in charge, the word of God comes to John, son of Zechariah. Where is John when it comes?

cards.text: John goes into all the region around the Jordan and starts preaching. One man, one river, one message.

cards.question: Around the Jordan, John preaches a baptism of ___ for the forgiveness of sins.

cards.text: Luke says this is just what was written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet. Isaiah wrote about a voice of one calling in the wilderness.

cards.question: Isaiah's voice in the wilderness calls out to prepare the ___ for the Lord and make straight paths for Him.

cards.text: Then Isaiah's picture turns into the BIGGEST road project you've ever seen: every valley filled in, every mountain and hill made low. And for once, road work isn't making anybody late.

cards.question: True or false: In Isaiah's picture of the road for the Lord, the rough ways are made smooth.
Then Isaiah's words end with a promise: all ___ will see God's salvation.

cards.text: Crowds are coming out to be baptized by John, so you'd expect a warm welcome. Not exactly.

cards.question: What does John call the crowds coming out to be baptized by him?

cards.text: Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and even the dead batteries in there with me never called me THAT. John asks who warned them to flee from the coming wrath, and tells them to produce fruit in keeping with repentance.

cards.question: John tells the crowds their lives need to show their repentance. What does he tell them not to say to themselves?

answers.text: We have Abraham as our father
We have Moses as our lawgiver
We have David as our king

cards.question: True or false: John tells the crowds that God can raise up children for Abraham out of these stones.

cards.text: Then John gives them a picture to think about: the axe lies ready at the root of the trees.

cards.question: In John's picture of the axe at the root, what happens to every tree that does not produce good fruit?

answers.text: It's cut down and thrown into the fire
It's given one more year to grow
It's dug up and planted somewhere else

cards.text: John just called them a brood of vipers, and the crowds come right back with, "What then should we do?" Friend, I LIKE this crowd.

cards.question: John tells the crowds that whoever has two tunics should ___ with him who has none.
True or false: John tells the crowds that whoever has food should do the same as whoever has two tunics.

cards.text: Even tax collectors come to be baptized, and they ask John what they should do. That's like the guy who writes parking tickets walking up to you and asking, "How do I do better?"

cards.question: The tax collectors ask John what they should do. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Collect no more than you're authorized
Give half of what you collect away
Leave your tax booth for good

cards.text: Then some soldiers step up with the same question: "And what should we do?"

cards.question: John tells the soldiers not to take money by force or false accusation, and to be ___ with their ___.

cards.text: By now the people are waiting expectantly. And everybody's wondering the same thing about John, deep in their hearts.

cards.question: What are the people all wondering in their hearts about John?

answers.text: If John could be the Christ
If John was Elijah come back

cards.text: John answers all of them: he baptizes with water, but One more powerful than he is will come. Then John tells them exactly where he stands next to that One.

cards.question: How does John describe himself next to the One more powerful who is coming?

answers.text: Not worthy to untie His sandal straps
Not worthy to carry His walking staff
Not worthy to stand inside His house

cards.text: That One, John says, will baptize them with the Holy Spirit and with fire. John keeps pointing away from himself, and me? I get ONE compliment on a batch and I brag for a WEEK.
Then John gives a harvest picture: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor.

cards.question: True or false: In John's harvest picture, the chaff is gathered into the barn along with the wheat.

cards.text: The wheat gets gathered into His barn, but He burns up the chaff with unquenchable fire. Fire AGAIN, friend, just like those trees with no good fruit.

With these and many other exhortations, John proclaims the good news to the people. And he doesn't stop at the crowds: he rebukes Herod the tetrarch about his brother's wife and all the evils he had done.

cards.question: John rebukes Herod the tetrarch about his brother's wife, ___.
John has rebuked Herod the tetrarch. How does Herod respond?

answers.text: He locks John up in prison
He asks John what he should do
He sends John out of Galilee

findings.problem: The setup only says that John is preaching; it gives no context about repentance or turning from sin. A new baker can only recognize or guess the unseen BSB wording that completes "a baptism of ___ for the forgiveness of sins," rather than reason out the blank's meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards establishes that Isaiah's promise expands to all humanity. In particular, the baker has no basis for choosing "humanity" over "Israel," so this is a guess at the unseen wording of the line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The preceding story card deliberately withholds the wife's name, and no earlier card supplies a clue from which "Herodias" can be inferred. The blank therefore asks for an unseen name rather than testing meaning the baker can reason out.
